title: Pardons Dwight and Steven Hammond
description_short: Trump granted pardons to Oregon ranchers Dwight and Steven Hammond, convicted of arson on federal lands.
description_medium: Trump pardoned Oregon ranchers Dwight and Steven Hammond, a father and son convicted of arson after fires burned on federal land. The Associated Press reported that they were resentenced to five years after an appeals court required a mandatory minimum, and that Trump called the sentences unjust. The pardon was issued July 10, 2018.
description_long: Dwight and Steven Hammond, an Oregon father and son who ranched on public land, were convicted of arson after fires spread onto federal property. The Associated Press reported that a jury acquitted them on most charges and that the Hammonds admitted setting fires. After an appeals court required a five-year mandatory minimum, they were resentenced and returned to prison. President Donald Trump granted them full pardons on July 10, 2018; the White House described their sentences as unjust. Their case had become politically charged after armed protesters occupied the Malheur National Wildlife Refuge in 2016 in support of the ranchers. The clemency ended the Hammonds’ federal criminal consequences but did not erase the history of the convictions or the debate over the mandatory sentence. The input record is dated May 29, 2018, and its linked archived White House statement concerns five different clemency recipients in 2019. The date and source association must be corrected before the entry can be treated as complete.

title: Appoints Richard Grenell Acting DNI
description_short: Trump appointed Richard Grenell as acting director of national intelligence, bypassing Senate confirmation.
description_medium: On February 19, 2020, Donald Trump named Richard Grenell acting director of national intelligence. The acting designation meant Grenell would take the post without Senate confirmation. House Speaker Nancy Pelosi criticized the move as sidestepping the Senate’s constitutional confirmation role, while the administration installed him in an interim capacity rather than submitting a permanent nomination.
description_long: Donald Trump named Richard Grenell acting director of national intelligence on February 19, 2020. Grenell, then the U.S. ambassador to Germany, was selected to lead the Office of the Director of National Intelligence in an acting capacity. That designation allowed him to assume the job without undergoing Senate confirmation as a permanent nominee. House Speaker Nancy Pelosi objected that the appointment sidestepped the Senate’s constitutional role and said Grenell could not be confirmed even by a Republican-controlled Senate. The acting title is central to the dispute: Trump did not place a Senate-confirmed nominee in the post, but the source describes Grenell as an acting official rather than reporting a formal ruling that the appointment was unlawful. The choice put a political appointee with diplomatic experience in charge of the intelligence community and renewed debate over how long senior national-security positions could be filled on an interim basis without a confirmation vote.
